catalog_quote: 2. Phonèmes supra-segmentaires. Le kpálá est un parler à tons: haut, moyen et bas; puis ascendant et descendant. H/B: búma (coeur) buma (kapokier), dó (lance) do (parole); H/M: nsɔ́ (animal) nsɔ̓ (queue); B/M: zro (laver) zrɔ̓ (sorgho); A/D: ikɔ̌tɔ (sortir) ikɔ̂tɔ (descendre), yǎ (parent) yâ (éléphant). [p. 328; the mid-tone mark is the apostrophe-shaped sign defined p. 323 'M, ’: ton moyen'] — Au niveau suprasegmentaire, le kpala présente 5 valeurs tonales: le haut, le moyen, le bas, l'ascendant et le descendant. [p. 321] — N. B.: Le texte a bénéficié de l'économie du ton bas [p. 323]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: 2. Suprasegmental phonemes. Kpala is a tone language: high, mid and low; plus rising and falling. H/L: búma 'heart' / buma 'kapok tree', dó 'spear' / do 'speech'; H/M: nsó 'animal' / nsɔ̀ 'tail'; L/M: zro 'to wash' / zrō 'sorghum'; rising/falling: ikǒtɔ 'to go out' / ikôtɔ 'to go down', yǎ 'parent' / yâ 'elephant'. — At the suprasegmental level, Kpala shows 5 tonal values: high, mid, low, rising and falling.
new_statements.citation: Ebanda wa Kalema. 1991. Le kpala, un parler oubanguien. Annales Æquatoria 12: 321-330.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only description of Kpala is a 10-page phonological sketch of the Libenge dialect. Its suprasegmental section describes a lexical tone system (three level tones H, M, L plus rising and falling contours) with word-level minimal pairs; it says nothing at all about stress or accent, so no stress rule can be stated. The tonal diacritics on the examples in the page scan are approximate transcriptions of a poor scan.
new_statements.exceptions: None; p. 323 note: 'Le texte a bénéficié de l'économie du ton bas' (low tone is left unmarked in the text).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone on isolated citation forms (minimal pairs of nouns and verbs); dialect of Libenge (Sud-Ubangi, then Zaire), single informant Gbiandu Amunakpanya-Mango from the Kala Protestant mission.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the Libenge (Sud-Ubangi, DRC) dialect of Kpala from one informant from the Kala mission; the author also lists Kpala villages in the Bosobolo, Mobayi-Mbongo, Businga and Kungu zones. Glottolog kpal1241 has no dialect nodes. Wikipedia treats Kpala as a variety of Monzombo (Glottolog monz1253 is a family node 'Monzomboic'). The article's own spelling in running text is 'kpálá'.

tone_statements.citation: Mfouhou, Chrisnah Renaudot & Sara Pacchiarotti. 2025. A sketch of the phonology and morphosyntax of Kpálà ('Ubangi', Mundu-Baka, DRC). Africana Linguistica 31: 107-154. Leuven: Peeters / Tervuren: Royal Museum for Central Africa. DOI 10.2143/AL.31.0.3295060; hdl 1854/LU-01KE6XJPG2C31SD5Q3G1EJ4CNP (Ghent University Academic Bibliography, open-access published version, PDF 1.02 MB).
tone_statements.quote: In Kpálà, tone has a considerable functional load both lexically and grammatically (see Section 3.2). There are three underlying tones in Kpálà: H(igh), M(id) and L(ow). … In addition to the three level tones H, M, L, Ebanda wa Kalema (1991) posits the existence of two underlying contour tones, R(ising) and F(alling). In our data, we only have evidence of surface contour tones in cases of vowel syncopation, whenever the tone of the syncopated vowel is different from the tone of the remaining stem vowel … In this case, the surface F(alling) contour is underlyingly a sequence of H and L.
tone_statements.summary: Three underlying level tones H, M, L with minimal pairs; surface rising/falling contours analysed as LH/HL sequences (tonal stability under syncope); a melodic replacive L tone marks past tenses.
